title: Resolve bot battles as soon as the player is done

hypothesis.statement: Removing the non-interactive wait for the bot's simulated finish (up to 85/140/230s by difficulty) will increase the share of players whose bot battles reach the result screen.

variants.description: Current behaviour: after a wrong (single-question) or imperfect (multi-question) submission, the player waits until the bot's scheduled finish time.

As soon as the player has submitted their final answer, the bot's result is drawn immediately from the same accuracy distribution (BOT_ACCURACY) and the result screen is shown. Win/loss probabilities are unchanged; only the wait is removed. Quant Battle is not affected.

primaryMetric.definition: Share of exposed units whose bot battles all reached the result screen (no game_abandoned with opponent_type=bot).

guardrails.definition: Share of exposed units with a game_abandoned before their first submission in any game.
Share of exposed units active again 1-7 days after first exposure.
Share of exposed units with at least one client error (Sentry event tagged with experiment variant).

feasibility.note: Unknown until GA4 traffic is available.

evaluationPlan: Analyse only units with an experiment_exposure event (intent-to-treat from first exposure).
Daily: sample-ratio-mismatch check (chi-square, p < 0.001 pauses the experiment).
Daily: guardrails via always-valid mSPRT p-values; any significant harm recommends revert immediately.
Primary metric is not interpreted before 14 days and 167 units per arm.
After that, stop when the always-valid p < 0.05, or at 665 units per arm / 42 days, whichever first; reaching the cap without significance is "inconclusive".
Report effect size with confidence interval, not just significance. A human makes the final keep/revert decision.
codeChangeOutline: server/index.js startBotMatch: keep the bot resolution in a named function; in the treatment arm call it (and clear the pending timers) from submit_answer once the human has finished.
socket auth: accept anonId in handshake auth; server computes the variant with agent/src/flags/assign.js (same file served to the client as /flags.js).
match_found payload: include { experiment_id, variant } so the client can fire experiment_exposure once.
Default to control whenever the experiment is not live (unapproved, edited after approval, or missing anonId).
risks: Faster losses might feel abrupt; watch premature_exit_rate.
The bot's "thinking" status messages no longer appear in treatment.

prerequisites.description: Metric "Bot vs human battle share" is measurable (instrumentation shipped and verified)
Metric "Abandonment conditional on question difficulty and position" is measurable (instrumentation shipped and verified)
Consent Mode default-deny in place; experiment events only fire with analytics consent
experiment_exposure event emitted with experiment_id and variant
Treatment code reviewed and merged behind the flag (default = control)
